PullRequest.Title: copilot: harden Snippy tokenization and request validation
PullRequest.Body:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

Fixes #331807

## Summary

The reported Snippy `Match` response requires 110 lexemes, while the existing client checks use 65. This change keeps the 110-lexeme mitigation and hardens request construction for accepted inline completions and next-edit suggestions.

- Share one tokenizer and request builder between both paths, with pinned Unicode character data rather than runtime-dependent categories.
- Select genuine preceding context without reversing UTF-16 or splitting tokens, including identifiers and separator runs that merge across the insertion boundary.
- Skip sources below the minimum, oversized insertions, and ill-formed Unicode with diagnostics. Do not pad, truncate, or rewrite the insertion.
- Catch and log remaining next-edit failures, including malformed or failed `FilesForMatch` responses.
- Anchor expanded inline citations at the selected context start. Preserve successful next-edit citation details when another lookup fails, then propagate the failures.
- Add request-level boundary, Unicode, offset, and error-handling regression tests. Address the review comment by checking the same long input twice before the short input; a mutation check confirms that the updated assertion detects the original missing-reset regression.

## Compatibility

The minimum remains index-specific. Service-owner confirmation of compatibility across supported routed indexes, or explicit acceptance of the lost 65-109-lexeme coverage on lower-minimum indexes, is still required before merging. This is not threshold negotiation and does not claim to eliminate every Snippy HTTP 400. Remaining-failure handling is separate from avoiding invalid requests.

## Validation

Commands below run from `extensions/copilot` unless stated otherwise.

- `npm run test:unit -- src\platform\snippy\test\common\snippyCompute.spec.ts src\extension\completions-core\vscode-node\lib\src\snippy\test\requests.spec.ts src\extension\inlineEdits\test\node\nextEditProviderSpeculative.spec.ts --reporter=dot` - **120 passed, 2 pre-existing skips**. Successful unchanged request/acceptance results were reused after the review-only assertion refinement.
- `npm run test:unit -- src\platform\snippy\test\common\snippyCompute.spec.ts --reporter=dot` - **20 passed** after that refinement.
- `node --import tsx .\node_modules\mocha\bin\mocha.js --ui tdd src\extension\completions-core\vscode-node\lib\src\snippy\test\compute.test.ts --reporter dot` - **22 passed** after that refinement; after removing the redundant re-export and duplicate suite, the same command **passed all 11 remaining helper tests**.
- `npm run test:unit -- src\extension\completions-core\vscode-node\lib\src\snippy\test\requests.spec.ts --reporter=dot` - **59 passed** after the re-export cleanup.
- From the repository root: `npm run eslint -- extensions\copilot\src\platform\snippy\test\common\snippyCompute.spec.ts extensions\copilot\src\extension\completions-core\vscode-node\lib\src\snippy\test\compute.test.ts` - **passed** for the two refined tests; prior targeted lint results for unchanged implementation files were reused.
- The normal `npm run -s precommit` hook completed successfully. Its filters reported zero applicable hygiene files, so this is not claimed as additional source validation.

No production Match endpoints were called. Deployment-wide compatibility remains unverified; full server HTTP-handler boundary validation still requires a supported test environment.

### Code OSS regression validation at `59f76f2baa6a9a889795710ce09e850c6ecd1f82`

**82 acceptance scenarios and 4 additional normal-window notification checks passed** in Code OSS **1.145.0 Dev, Windows x64**, using Electron **43.8.3**.

The real editor's acceptance callbacks exercised the production inline-completion and next-edit acceptance, Snippy, citation, and notification implementations. Suggestions and authentication were deterministic fixtures; all Snippy traffic was restricted to loopback. Emitted request sources were checked with an independent tokenizer oracle and strict request decoder. Matching/index responses were simulated, not production-service responses.

Covered:

- Both paths at 1, 64, 65, 109, 110, 111, 220, 3,000, and 3,001 lexemes; a next-edit deletion also verified that no empty request is sent.
- Genuine preceding-context expansion, exact combined minimum, insufficient context, and long suffixes that must not make a short insertion eligible.
- Identifier and separator joins, supplementary Unicode, surrogate-safe slicing, Unicode-version differences, long identifiers, whitespace/CRLF, and representative code.
- Exact accepted text, partial-word acceptance, rejection, undo, deletion, existing annotations, and blocking mode.
- Reference output and licensing, first-match notifications, their reference-opening actions, and duplicate-notification suppression.
- HTTP 400, HTTP 500, and malformed responses from both `Match` and `FilesForMatch`, with recovery and no unhandled rejection in the checked acceptance paths.

Commands and results, from the repository root unless noted:

- `npm run build-fast` - **passed**, preparing the full client, built-in extensions, and Copilot.
- `node .build\snippy-ui\build-harness.cjs` - **passed**, building the temporary validation extension from the current production sources.
- From `extensions/copilot`: `.\node_modules\.bin\tsc.cmd --noEmit --project .build\snippy-ui-extension\tsconfig.json` - **passed**.
- `node test\scenario\out\runScenario.js .build\snippy-ui\scenario.cjs --dev --extensionDevelopmentPath C:\repos\vscode.worktrees\fix-snippy-validation\extensions\copilot\.build\snippy-ui-extension` - **passed**, 82 acceptance cases plus startup/summary checks, with `SNIPPY_UI_RUN=final` and no case filter.
- `node .build\snippy-ui\normal-toasts.cjs` - **passed**, four checks in a normal window without the smoke-test driver. This separate run was necessary because the scenario runner intentionally suppresses notification toasts.

Captioned recordings and per-case evidence were retained locally; temporary harnesses, profiles, and workspaces were removed. The results are scoped to this revision and these scenarios, not a blanket claim that every possible regression is excluded.

**Still unverified:** supported deployments' loaded minimums and the 65-109-lexeme coverage tradeoff; full server HTTP-handler boundary checks; live model-provider flows; macOS/Linux UI behavior; screen-reader use; performance under load. No production Match calls or deployment changes were made.

### Citation review follow-up at `d28c58c69b245e361b3fbf1dca3da60c7cda4cba`

Addressed the two additional citation review findings:

- Expanded inline Match responses now use the selected source's start offset, keeping citation offsets, line/column positions, and cited document text consistent. Regression cases cover 1, 65, 90, and 109-token insertions after CRLF and supplementary Unicode context.
- Next-edit reference lookups settle before results are processed. Successful citations retain their license and reference details when another lookup fails. A single failure retains its original error; multiple failures are propagated together after successful citations are logged.

The new tests demonstrated **8 failures before the production edits**. After the fixes:

- From `extensions/copilot`: `npm run test:unit -- src\extension\completions-core\vscode-node\lib\src\snippy\test\requests.spec.ts --reporter=dot` - **71 passed**, including mixed HTTP, malformed and structured failures, plus multiple-failure detail preservation.
- From `extensions/copilot`: `.\node_modules\.bin\tsc.cmd --noEmit --project tsconfig.json` - **passed**.
- From `extensions/copilot`: `npm run compile` - **passed**, including Node, web and worker bundles.
- From the repository root: `npm run eslint -- extensions\copilot\src\extension\completions-core\vscode-node\lib\src\snippy\handlePostInsertion.ts extensions\copilot\src\platform\snippy\common\snippyServiceImpl.ts extensions\copilot\src\extension\completions-core\vscode-node\lib\src\snippy\test\requests.spec.ts` - **passed** for all three changed files.

The earlier 82+4 Code OSS results remain scoped to `59f76f2baa6`; this follow-up was validated with the focused regression suite, type-checking, compilation and linting, not another full GUI run. Tokenization thresholds and source selection were unchanged.

### Standalone package follow-up

Declare the pinned Unicode runtime dependency in chat-lib's own manifest and lockfile, not only the parent extension, and supply its verified upstream MIT license through the existing license-override mechanism.

The missing-dependency failure was reproduced in a throwaway extraction with all ancestor `node_modules` directories removed. After the repair, `npm run build` **passed** and `npm test` **passed all 19 chat-lib tests** in that same isolated package. A compiled-module smoke check also confirmed that it resolves the Unicode package from its own dependencies. The packaging follow-up's normal pre-commit hook passed and checked one applicable metadata file.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The static import chain from both extension entry points through common service registration to `snippyServiceImpl` and `snippyCompute` is explicit, and the added imports plus `new RegExp` prove eager regex construction. The exact millisecond cost depends on runtime and bundled pattern size, so severity is low rather than uncertain causality.
Findings.PerformanceResource: bundle bytes, CPU work to parse/compile five Unicode regexes, and four intermediate RegExp objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is fixed but unconditional once per node or web extension-host bundle load, so it affects all activations rather than scaling only with Snippy usage.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased startup latency from synchronous regex parsing and compilation on the extension activation path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The module created one compact property-escape tokenizer RegExp; no external Unicode category regex modules or intermediate category RegExp objects were loaded and compiled.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Extension bundle initialization now evaluates four Unicode-category regex modules and synchronously parses a fifth combined Unicode regex before any Snippy request is made.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 6-9 add four static `.../regex.mjs` imports and RIGHT line 12 reads each imported RegExp's source to compile another combined RegExp. `snippyServiceImpl` is statically imported by the common services module, which is imported by both node and web extension entry points, so these module initializers run when the extension bundle loads.
Findings.Title: Defer the pinned Unicode regexes until Snippy is used
Findings.Impact: Every Copilot extension activation, including sessions that never accept an inline completion or next edit, pays additional extension-host startup CPU and retains the intermediate RegExp objects; on slower desktop and web extension hosts this lengthens activation/module initialization.
Findings.Evidence: `extensions/copilot/.esbuild.mts` bundles dependencies and does not externalize `@unicode/unicode-15.0.0`; both node and web service modules statically import the common `vscode/services.ts`, which statically imports `SnippyService`, which statically imports this module. Each `regex.mjs` supplies a category RegExp (its `.source` is consumed), then line 12 constructs the actual tokenizer RegExp. This performs four unnecessary intermediate regex compilations plus the final compilation during bundle evaluation.
Findings.Recommendation: Generate/store the pinned Unicode-15 category sources as one combined pattern and lazily compile a single tokenizer on first Snippy use (or otherwise keep the generated tokenizer module off the activation import path).

Scenarios.Scenario: Node and web Copilot extension activation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Static entry-point imports reach common service registration, `SnippyService`, and `snippyCompute` before `activate` runs, so the added Unicode regex module evaluation is on the extension activation/module-load critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed cost per extension-host bundle load, determined by the four Unicode category pattern sizes; it applies to every activation regardless of Snippy use.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Module evaluation and RegExp construction are synchronous and serialized on the extension-host thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold extension-host load evaluates the bundled module graph and constructs the Unicode regex objects; subsequent accesses in the same host reuse module singletons. A new extension host pays the cost again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both extension entry points statically reach the changed module, esbuild bundles the dependency, and the changed top-level imports plus `new RegExp` execute unconditionally.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository proves five eager RegExp constructions but does not include built bundle byte deltas or activation timings; exact milliseconds vary by Node/browser runtime and device.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity eager startup regression: four category regexes and a fifth combined tokenizer are parsed/compiled for all users instead of only when Snippy is used.

Scenarios.Scenario: Accepting an inline completion or panel completion and checking citations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Ghost-text acceptance launches post-insertion citation work detached from applying the edit; panel code also receives a synchronous `postInsertionTasks` return because citation work is invoked without awaiting it. Tokenization and network therefore do not block insertion, but consume extension-host CPU shortly afterward and gate citation availability.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Snippy Match request containing the selected completion/context source
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per eligible accepted insertion; sources are accepted at 110-3000 lexemes, with up to 110 preceding lexemes selected for short insertions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same scenario issued one Match request, using the prior 65-lexeme minimum and tokenizer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the initial edit-application path, but gates citation discovery and consumes background extension-host/network capacity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: FilesForMatch lookup for each Match snippet cursor
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: S concurrent requests for S returned snippets after one successful Match; failures do not create retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-snippet concurrent FilesForMatch fan-out existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off insertion; all lookups must settle before citations are processed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Synchronous tokenization grows with completion lexemes up to 3001 and, for short completions, with the document prefix scanned to find the last 110 lexemes. Network fan-out grows with effective snippet count S.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Match request is awaited first; if it returns S snippets, S FilesForMatch requests are started together and joined with `Promise.all`. The diff does not add a limiter or change this fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no Match or FilesForMatch result cache/coalescing on this path. Regex state is module-cached; each accepted insertion is tokenized anew. Network behavior is cold per eligible acceptance.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call ordering, request cardinality, and detached execution; surrounding callers and the changed request builder establish the path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Accepted insertion lengths and snippet counts vary; the 3000-lexeme boundary is explicitly supported, but typical completions are shorter. No timing data establishes a separate user-visible regression from the bounded duplicate token scan.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: request cardinality and concurrency are unchanged, raised validation bounds are intentional, and the duplicate bounded scan lacks evidence of material impact beyond the separately reported unconditional startup work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Accepting a next-edit suggestion and running the Snippy check
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `handleAcceptance` fire-and-forgets `runSnippy`; synchronous source construction runs immediately until `fetchMatch` yields, while Match and subsequent reference lookups are off the acceptance return path. The new await is inside the detached helper and exists to catch/log failures.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Snippy Match request for the accepted next-edit source
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per eligible accepted next edit; deletions, short sources without enough context, invalid Unicode, and sources over 3000 lexemes are skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One Match request was already issued for eligible next-edit acceptances, with the old tokenizer/minimum.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The network wait is detached from acceptance; only synchronous request construction occurs before the first await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: FilesForMatch lookup for every returned snippet
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: S concurrent lookups for S snippets; no retries or duplicate lookups are introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same S lookups were started concurrently under `Promise.all`; an early rejection returned sooner but did not cancel the other already-started requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Detached from edit acceptance; now all settle before successful citations are logged and any aggregate error is propagated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU scales with accepted edit/document context size under the 3000-lexeme guard; boundary fan-out scales with returned snippet count S.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Match request precedes S parallel FilesForMatch requests. `Promise.allSettled` now waits for all S results before propagating failures, but it launches no additional calls and preserves the existing aggregate burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No request cache or in-flight coalescing is used. The tokenizer singleton is warm after module load, but source construction runs for every accepted next edit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the acceptance caller, fire-and-forget helper, synchronous pre-await source construction, and network sequence are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The service response snippet count and network tail latency vary. `allSettled` can extend failure-reporting lifetime to the slowest request, but the requests and retained handlers already existed and the work is detached, so evidence does not support a material performance finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff does not increase boundary count or concurrency, and waiting for all already-launched lookups is not on the edit-application critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Installing and building the standalone @vscode/chat-lib package
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Dependency installation must complete before chat-lib compilation/use. At runtime, extracted CommonJS output resolves the declared dependency directly rather than relying on an ancestor installation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download `@unicode/unicode-15.0.0@2.1.0` during a cold npm install
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One package tarball per cold dependency installation, normally zero registry downloads when a valid npm cache is warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: chat-lib did not declare or download this Unicode data package.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks first installation/build of the standalone SDK package.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract/install the Unicode package into the standalone dependency tree
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One package extraction per fresh install; effective file/byte count is not stated in repository metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Unicode package files were installed for chat-lib.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of npm install before chat-lib can build or run.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One-time cost scales with the dependency tarball and extracted file sizes, not user data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrency is controlled by npm; this diff adds one direct package fetch/install unit and no application-level limiter or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A cold npm install downloads and extracts the new Unicode package; a warm npm cache can avoid the registry download but still resolves/installs it into a fresh dependency tree. Runtime module caching applies after process load.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the cold install adds one network/package extraction boundary; low evidence for magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The lockfile gives integrity and version but not compressed/unpacked size, so repository evidence cannot establish material install-time or disk impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the direct dependency repairs standalone resolution, and the supplied diff lacks size evidence needed to classify the single added install boundary as a material performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files and traced activation, both acceptance paths, Snippy network fan-out, tokenization bounds, and standalone package installation. Submitted one low-severity eager-startup finding; no other changed mechanism had sufficient evidence of material performance impact.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
